description.en: Turn a repo link into a one-minute 9:16 terminal-style showcase. Stars and the install command come from GitHub, not from the model.
description.vi: Biến link repo thành video giới thiệu dọc 9:16 dài khoảng một phút, phong cách terminal. Số sao và lệnh cài lấy từ GitHub, không qua mô hình.

sceneFields.name: kicker
sceneFields.rule: two or three words naming what the scene is about, uppercase, shown small above the content

doc.example: {"headline":"HTTP, WITHOUT THE CEREMONY","subline":"A tiny router that gets out of your way.","badgeText":"TRENDING"}
doc.when: The opening of a product or project video: one uppercase line that says what it is, one softer line under it, and a small badge. The star count is added from data.

headline.hint: what it is, six words at most; it is shown uppercase

subline.hint: one plain sentence on who it is for or what it removes

badgeText.hint: a short label such as TRENDING or NEW RELEASE

code.source: stars

doc.example: {"headline":"Ship video from a graph","body":"Wire a source to a script, a voice and an engine."}
doc.when: One idea on screen: a headline and at most one supporting line. Use it for openings, transitions and closings; not for lists or numbers.

headline.hint: up to six words, title case

body.hint: one sentence, or leave it out

doc.example: {"title":"Routes as plain functions","detail":"A handler is a function of request and response; nothing to subclass, nothing to register."}
doc.when: One capability per scene, three to five in a row. A short title and one sentence that says what it does for the user; no marketing adjectives.

title.hint: the capability in three to five words

detail.hint: one concrete sentence on what it does or removes

doc.example: {"headline":"Three lines to a running server","featureHighlights":["Routes as plain functions","Middleware you can read","Zero config, zero build"]}
doc.when: Showing what a developer tool does: a headline over a terminal window with exactly three feature lines. The install command and repo name are added from data.

featureHighlights.hint: three short feature lines, verbs first, no full stops

code.source: $

doc.example: {"number":69417,"label":"stars on GitHub","caption":"Used in production by teams of every size."}
doc.when: One figure that proves the point, filling the frame, with a label and one line of context. The figure comes from data when bound; never invent one.

number.hint: the figure; filled from data when bound

label.hint: what the figure counts, two to four words

caption.hint: one line of context, or leave it out

doc.example: {"headline":"Ship your next API on it","callToActionText":"Star the repo, read the docs, open your first issue.","buttonText":"Star on GitHub"}
doc.when: The closing of a project video: a card with the headline, one inviting sentence, and one button. The repo link is added from data.

headline.hint: the invitation in a few words

callToActionText.hint: one sentence saying what to do next

buttonText.hint: the button label, two or three words

doc.example: {"title": "Nodes, not timelines"}
doc.when: One line and nothing else, as large as the frame allows. Openings, turns, and the last word; never for detail.

title.hint: three to six words that stand alone

doc.example: {"title": "Everything is a node", "body": "The look, the voice, the engine: all data on the canvas."}
doc.when: A headline and one line, centred, with light behind them. For the idea the whole video turns on; softer than a big statement, calmer than a card.

title.hint: the idea in four to eight words

body.hint: one sentence that makes it concrete

doc.example: {"title": "Out of the box", "points": ["Typed ports", "Partial re-runs", "Karaoke captions"]}
doc.when: Two to five short items that are all true at once: what you get, what is included, what it handles. Each item gets a tick.

title.hint: what the list is, three to five words

points.hint: two to five items, each under six words

doc.example: {"title": "From link to video", "points": ["Paste the repo link", "Press run", "Download the MP4"]}
doc.when: Two to five things done in order: a setup, a workflow, a recipe. Each item is numbered; the order is the point.

points.hint: two to five steps, each a short imperative

doc.example: {"title": "Renders anywhere", "points": ["MP4", "1080p to 4K", "9:16 and 16:9", "Subtitles"]}
doc.when: Four to six short items that belong together but have no order: capabilities, integrations, formats. Tiles in two columns.

title.hint: what the tiles have in common

points.hint: four to six items, one to three words each

doc.example: {"title": "Built with", "points": ["TypeScript", "React", "GSAP", "ffmpeg"]}
doc.when: Words, not sentences: topics, languages, integrations, tags. Three to eight chips under a short title.

points.hint: three to eight single words or short names

doc.example: {"code": "npm create nodecine@latest", "body": "One command, no config."}
doc.when: One command in a terminal window, with an optional line saying what it does. For install, run and build steps when the command itself is the message.

code.hint: the command, without a prompt character

body.hint: what the command does, one short line

title.hint: a window title, two or three words

code.source: $

doc.example: {"quote": "It replaced a week of After Effects with an afternoon.", "attribution": "a happy user"}
doc.when: Somebody's words, verbatim, with who said them: a maintainer, a user, a review. Only when there is a real quote to show.

code.source: “

doc.example: {"label": "Note", "body": "Renders run on your machine; nothing is uploaded."}
doc.when: A boxed note with a small label: a warning, a tip, a limitation, a requirement. One or two sentences; the label says which kind.

label.hint: the kind of note: Note, Tip, Requires, Limitation

doc.example: {"label": "Open source", "title": "MIT licensed, forever", "body": "Use it in anything, no strings."}
doc.when: A small label over a large title: a section opener, a name and what it is, a category and its example. Add a line only if it is needed.

label.hint: two to four words, the category

title.hint: the headline, up to eight words

doc.example: {"label": "v0.1", "title": "First render", "body": "A node graph became an MP4 for the first time."}
doc.when: One moment on a path: a version, a milestone, a phase. A label with the when, a title with the what, a line of detail; a dot on a vertical line.

label.hint: when or which: a version, a date, a phase

title.hint: what happened, three to six words

doc.example: {"number": "98", "label": "percent smaller", "body": "Compared with the previous build."}
doc.when: One figure inside a ring, with what it is and one line of context. Counts, percentages, sizes; when the number should feel measured rather than shouted.

number.hint: the figure; the label says the unit

label.hint: what the number is, two to five words

doc.example: {"title": "Read the docs", "source": "nodecine.dev/docs"}
doc.when: A headline with where to find it: a repo, a site, a handle. The link is added from data. For "go here" moments that are not the closing call to action.

title.hint: what is there, three to six words

source.hint: the address or handle; filled from data when bound

doc.example: {"title": "Video from a graph", "body": "Wire nodes, press run, get an MP4.", "points": ["No timeline", "Runs locally", "Any language"]}
doc.when: A headline, a sentence and two to four supporting points on one card: the summary scene, the "in short" before or after the detail.

title.hint: the summary in three to six words

points.hint: two to four short supporting points

params.prompt: A one-minute showcase of this software project for developers scrolling past. Open with what it is, walk through what it does, show how to install it, prove it with the numbers, say who it is for, then invite them in. Confident, specific, no hype; every claim must come from the facts. The install command, the star count and the link are added later from GitHub — do not write them.

beats.brief: What it is, in one uppercase line, for a developer scrolling past. Add a two-word badge label.
The problem it solves, in one plain sentence.
One capability per scene, taken from the README; concrete, no adjectives.
How to get started: the headline says how little it takes; the three lines are what you get. The three lines are three short points.
The star count as the proof, with a label and one line of context.
Who it is for, and when to reach for it.
Invite them to star or contribute. Give the button a two-word label.
